slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A conditional is a statement "If p, then q." p is the hypothesis and q is the conclusion.

Converse: if q, then p. Inverse: if not p, then not q. Contrapositive: if not q, then not p.

A conditional and its contrapositive are always both true or both false. The converse and inverse also match each other, but they can be false even when the original is true. "If a figure is a square, then it has four sides" is true; its converse "If a figure has four sides, then it is a square" is false.
